 Song Review: ATEEZ – Drip
 Posted on October 22, 2026 by Nick 22 Comments 
 ATEEZ have commanded a large fanbase for years now, but this year they find themselves with an equally large public hit on their hands. I still don’t get how Bad turned into the sensation it did (the song just does nothing for me), but the group is now in a unique position to build upon that chart success with music that pulls casual fans deeper into their world. Ahead of a new album next month, pre-release Drip arrives as the first step toward that goal.
 When a group scores a big hit, they tend to try to replicate that same sensation in an even bigger and bolder way. That means doubling down on the qualities that made a song successful, which can result in extremely great or extremely bad material depending on the quality of that first hit. With Drip , ATEEZ have clearly learned that simple, monotonous hooks connect with the audience. Replace “bad, bad, bad” with “drip, bricks, whip” (one of those rhymes is not like the other) and you’ve got the basic idea. There’s a bit more going on here when it comes to flow, but the end product is more tiresome than exciting.
 Going back even further, Drip actually reminds me of their 2024 single Ice On My Teeth . That song had more interesting production to cover for its predictably braggadocious lyrics. With Drip , everything — from the instrumental to the resolution of each line — ends in the same place. It’s like kicking a can down the road. Something is moving, but nothing is moving with any purpose or destination.
